source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use an individualized, consistent bowel routine designed to produce predictable and effective elimination","B":"Wait for constipation or incontinence to occur, then treat each episode without a planned routine","C":"Rely only on fluid intake and avoid scheduled bowel care, rectal methods, or prescribed medications","D":"Use the same bowel schedule for every spinal cord injury regardless of function or personal goals"}}
source_row.rationale: Guidelines for neurogenic bowel after spinal cord injury recommend an individualized bowel program with a consistent schedule and interventions tailored to neurologic function, lifestyle, diet, fluids, and other needs.
source_row.source_detail: 2021 clinical practice guideline; Guiding Principles and Basic Bowel Management: predictable elimination and consistent individualized schedule; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: Consortium for Spinal Cord Medicine — Neurogenic Bowel Dysfunction CPG
source_row.stem: A client with spinal cord injury has neurogenic bowel dysfunction. Which approach best reflects an effective bowel-management program?
